summary: Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and was taught by Karin Preisendanz.

Marguerite E. Adiceam was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon and under Jean Filliozat. She taught at the Lycée Français de Pondichéry (1946–1954) and was a scientific member of École française d'Extrême-Orient (1966–1971).

Marguerite Lobsiger-Dellenbach was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Geneva by 1935. She served as Vice-Director (1947) and Director (1952–1967) of the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève.

Maria Byrski is an Indologist who studied under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz around 1955–1960. He served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw from circa 1990 to 1996 and taught Bożena Śliwczyńska and Danuta Stasik.

Maria Carlotta Avanzi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned master's degrees from the University of Turin and a doctorate from Kyoto University, serving as Associate Professor at Akita Prefectural University and Assistant Professor at ISEAS.

Maria Elisabeth Lulius van Goor was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who studied under Jacob Samuel Speyer and earned her Ph.D. at Leiden University. She was an attachée at EFEO (1922–1923) and taught Pāli at Leiden (1924).

Maria Gallas is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She earned a master's degree in philosophy from the National University of Distance Education (2019–2022) and became a PhD student at Universidad a Distancia de Madrid.

Maria Heim is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her BA from Reed College and PhD from Harvard University under Charles Hallisey. She was an Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Maria Vasylieva is a Buddhist studies scholar who holds degrees from Uppsala University, the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and International Buddhist College. In 2020, she became an Assistant Professor at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Maria Wilkins Smith was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Bryn Mawr College and completed her Ph.D. under Roland Grubb Kent at the University of Pennsylvania. She taught Latin at Temple University as Instructor and Assistant Professor (~1929–1947).

Marian Ury was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. From 1969 to 1995, she was a professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis.

Marianne Pieper studied at HHWP and Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held temporary professorships at the University of Hamburg (1990–1994) and University of Kassel (1994–1996), and served as C3-Professor of Sociology at Hamburg from 1996 to 2015.

Marianne Winder was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. Her career included posts at Nottingham, University of London, and the Wellcome Trust as Curator and Consultant.

Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Direktorin of the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).

Mariano José Saldanha was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado. He taught at Liceu Nacional Afonso de Albuquerque (1915–1929), the University of Lisbon (1929–1946), and was Subdirector at ISCSP (1929–1948).

Mariano Rampolla del Tindaro was an Indologist who studied under Oreste Nazari and attended the Pontifical Gregorian University. In 1933, he was appointed professor of Indian religious history and Sanskrit at the Pontifical Urban University.
Marie Brožová was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed her Ph.D. under the supervision of Josef Zubatý at Charles University by 1921.
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under the instruction of Sengaku Mayeda.

Marie Gatellier was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Jean Boisselier and André Bareau. From circa 1975 to 1993, she served as Chargée de recherche at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

id: P:Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys
summary: Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys was a Sinologist who studied under and later succeeded Stanislas Julien. He also taught Édouard Chavannes.
